text:
B: Alright. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah, fine. Gareth.
B: Darren.
A: Where are you, then?
B: Maidstone.
A: Oh, not far. I grew up in Bromley. Sister's in Sevenoaks now.
B: Yeah? Sevenoaks. Bit posh for me.
A: Bit posh for her, to be honest. What d'you do?
B: Bins. Council rounds. Six o'clock start.
A: Fair enough. I'm a structural engineer. Office in Farringdon, but I'm out on sites a fair bit.
B: Hard hat and a clipboard.
A: Pretty much, yeah. Mostly I'm telling contractors what they can't do.
B: Bet they love you.
A: Er, some of them. A couple have asked for someone else, to be fair.
B: I tell supervisors straight as well. Doesn't make you popular.
A: No. Gets the job done, though.
B: That's what I say.
A: Football?
B: Gillingham.
A: Ah. Palace, me.
B: You've got nothing to moan about, then.
A: I've got plenty. Manager should've gone in about October. We just sit there drawing nil-nil every other week and everyone acts like that's fine.
B: Try watching us. You'd want nil-nil.
A: Fair. D'you play?
B: Used to. Sunday league, when I was younger. Darts now. Pub league, Thursdays.
A: I played five-a-side every Wednesday till I did my knee in at thirty-nine. Still plays up when it's cold.
B: My back's the same. Lifting bins all day. Dunno how long it'll last, to be honest.
A: Can you move off the lifting?
B: Driving, if they put me through my HGV. They keep saying they will.
A: Keep on at them.
B: Yeah. I will.
A: Do you get a pint after the darts, then?
B: Couple of lagers. Price keeps going up though. Nearly six quid at my local.
A: Six? That's cheap. Try Walthamstow. And everything's craft, so it's seven-fifty for a pale ale in a jam jar.
B: I don't see the point of craft beer. It's just lager that costs more.
A: Nah, it's not, mate. Some of it's decent.
B: Some of it tastes like grapefruit.
A: Yeah, alright, some of it does. My GP says I should drink less anyway.
B: Mine says it every time. I just nod.
A: Same. Nod, and then—
